title: Exam Cram
subject: Lymphoid System
introMarkdown: **Quick Scan:** Short, bolded terms, definitions, pathways, comparisons, and high-yield associations. For fuller explanations switch to **Detailed Review**.
subtitle: Quick Scan

sections.title: Three Core Roles
sections.markdown:
**Three major lymphatic functions:**
- **Fluid recovery:** Returns excess **interstitial fluid and proteins** to venous blood; limits edema.
- **Immune defense:** Transports antigens/immune cells; supports surveillance and activation.
- **Dietary-fat transport:** Intestinal **lacteals** absorb chylomicrons; fat-rich **chyle** enters lymph.

- **Lymphopoiesis:** Production of lymphocytes.

**Rapid recall:** **Fluid balance + defense + fat absorption.**

sections.title: Lymph, Interstitial Fluid, and Capillaries
sections.markdown:
- **Blood plasma:** Fluid inside blood vessels.
- **Interstitial fluid:** Fluid surrounding tissue cells.
- **Lymph:** Interstitial fluid **after entering a lymphatic vessel**.
- **Initial lymphatic capillaries:** **Blind-ended**, highly permeable channels.
- **Overlapping endothelial flaps:** Open inward when tissue pressure rises; limit backflow.
- **Anchoring filaments:** Help hold capillaries open as surrounding tissue swells.
- **Basement membrane:** Incomplete/discontinuous in many initial lymphatic capillaries.

**Fluid route:** Blood plasma → interstitial fluid → lymphatic capillary (**lymph**) → collecting vessels → lymphatic trunks/ducts → venous blood.

**Contrast:** Blood capillaries connect blood circuits; initial lymphatics begin **blindly**.

sections.title: Valves and Lymph Propulsion
sections.markdown:
- **Collecting-vessel valves:** Prevent backward lymph flow.
- **Intrinsic lymphatic contractions:** Smooth muscle propels lymph.
- **Skeletal muscle pump:** Movement compresses nearby lymph vessels.
- **Respiratory pump:** Pressure changes with breathing favor lymph return.
- **Nearby arterial pulsations:** Can assist transport.
- **Lymphedema:** Swelling caused by inadequate lymph drainage.

**Key contrast:** **Entry flaps** admit tissue fluid into capillaries; **one-way valves** guide lymph through collecting vessels. No central lymphatic heart.

sections.title: Right Duct, Thoracic Duct, and Trunks
sections.markdown:
- **Right lymphatic duct:** Drains **right head/neck + right upper limb + right upper thorax** → **right venous angle**.
- **Thoracic duct:** Drains **the rest of the body** → **left venous angle**.
- **Venous angle:** Junction of **internal jugular + subclavian veins**.
- **Cisterna chyli:** Variable enlarged reservoir near thoracic duct origin; receives lower-body/intestinal lymph.

**Right-side trunks (3):** **Right jugular, right subclavian, right bronchomediastinal**.

**Thoracic-duct system — instructor's six named trunks:** **Left jugular, left subclavian, left bronchomediastinal, right lumbar, left lumbar, intestinal**.

**Memory rule:** **Right duct = right upper quadrant; thoracic duct = everything else.** Trunk joining patterns vary anatomically.

sections.title: Three Course-Defined Lymphoid Organs vs Tissues
sections.markdown:
- **Instructor's three encapsulated lymphoid organs:** **Lymph nodes, thymus, spleen**.
- **Lymphoid organ (lecture distinction):** Organized structure with connective-tissue capsule.
- **Lymphoid tissue:** Lymphocyte-rich areas/nodules, often without a separate complete capsule.
- **Primary lymphoid sites:** **Bone marrow** (B-cell development) + **thymus** (T-cell maturation).
- **Secondary lymphoid sites:** **Lymph nodes, spleen, MALT**; antigen encounters/activation.

**Exam caution:** Many texts also classify **bone marrow** as a primary lymphoid **organ**. For the lecture's “three organs,” use the instructor's named three.

sections.title: Lymph Node Flow and Identification
sections.markdown:
**Lymph pathway:** **Afferent vessel → subcapsular sinus → cortical/trabecular sinuses → medullary sinuses → efferent vessel**.

- **Afferent:** **Arrives**, usually at convex surface.
- **Efferent:** **Exits** at **hilum**.
- **Capsule:** Outer connective covering; **trabeculae** extend inward.
- **Hilum:** Vessel entry/exit indentation.
- **Outer cortex / follicles:** Mainly **B cells**.
- **Paracortex (deep cortex):** Mainly **T cells**.
- **Medullary cords:** Plasma cells, lymphocytes, macrophages.
- **Medullary sinuses:** Conduct lymph toward efferent vessels.
- **Germinal center:** Activated B-cell proliferation/selection in follicles.
- **Function:** **Filters lymph** and promotes antigen–lymphocyte encounters.

**Do not confuse:** The B-cell/T-cell regions are **locations**; lymph itself flows through **sinuses**.

sections.title: B Cells, T Cells, NK Cells, and Lymphopoiesis
sections.markdown:
- **B cells:** Develop/mature in **bone marrow**; **adaptive humoral** immunity.
- **T cells:** Precursors from marrow; mature/selected in **thymus**; **adaptive cell-mediated** immunity.
- **NK cells:** **Innate** killing of certain infected/abnormal cells.
- **CD4 helper T cells:** Coordinate immune responses; help B cells via signals.
- **CD8 cytotoxic T cells:** Kill appropriately recognized infected/abnormal host cells.
- **Regulatory T cells:** Suppress excessive/self-directed responses (older term: *suppressor*).
- **Plasma cells:** Differentiated B cells that **secrete antibodies**.
- **Memory B/T cells:** Faster responses after antigen re-exposure.

**Instructor clarification needed:** Guide asks for a **B-cell differentiation hormone**, but slides name **thymosins for T-cell development**, not a corresponding single B-cell hormone. **Do not substitute thymosin for B cells.**

sections.title: Thymus, Blood–Thymus Barrier, and Involution
sections.markdown:
- **Thymus location:** Anterior/superior **mediastinum**; prominent in childhood.
- **Lobes/lobules:** Two lobes; septa divide them into lobules.
- **Cortex:** Darker, lymphocyte-dense outer lobular region.
- **Medulla:** Paler inner region; contains **Hassall (thymic) corpuscles**.
- **Thymic epithelial cells:** Support T-cell development; participate in protective barriers.
- **Blood–thymus barrier:** Helps shield immature thymocytes in cortex.
- **Thymosins:** Lecture-associated thymic signals promoting **T-cell maturation**.
- **Positive/negative selection:** Support functional T cells and self-tolerance.
- **Thymic involution:** Age-related replacement of much thymic tissue by fat.

**Contrast:** **Thymus = T-cell training**, not filtration of afferent lymph like a node.

sections.title: Spleen: Red/White Pulp and Blood Path
sections.markdown:
- **Spleen:** Largest lymphoid organ; **left upper abdomen**, near ribs **9–11**.
- **Main function:** Filters **blood**; lymph nodes filter **lymph**.
- **White pulp:** Lymphocyte-rich; responds to blood-borne antigens.
- **Red pulp:** Removes aging/damaged **RBCs**; macrophages recover materials including iron.
- **Capsule/trabeculae:** Supporting connective tissue.
- **Hilum:** Splenic artery/vein entry/exit.
- **Splenectomy:** Surgical spleen removal.
- **Splenic rupture:** Can cause severe internal bleeding.

**Blood path:** Splenic artery → trabecular arteries → central arteries → smaller arterial branches → red-pulp cords/sinusoids → veins → splenic vein.

sections.title: Tonsils, Peyer's Patches, and MALT
sections.markdown:
- **MALT:** **Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue**; immune defense at mucosal surfaces.
- **GALT:** Gut-associated; **BALT:** bronchus-associated; **NALT:** nasal-associated.
- **Palatine tonsils:** Pair beside oropharynx.
- **Pharyngeal tonsil (adenoid):** Nasopharynx.
- **Lingual tonsillar tissue:** Tongue base.
- **Waldeyer's ring:** Tonsillar defenses around pharynx.
- **Peyer's patches:** Aggregated lymphoid nodules, especially in **ileum**.
- **Appendix:** Lymphoid-rich intestinal structure.
- **Germinal centers:** Activated B-cell proliferation and differentiation.

**Lecture count:** Five major tonsillar sites (2 palatine + 1 pharyngeal + 2 lingual), though lingual tissue is more variable anatomically.

sections.title: Seven Nonspecific Defenses — Instructor's Exact List
sections.markdown:
**Seven innate/nonspecific defenses — instructor's list:**
1. **Physical barriers:** Skin and mucosa prevent entry.
2. **Phagocytes:** Neutrophils/macrophages ingest threats.
3. **Immunological surveillance:** **NK cells** attack some abnormal cells.
4. **Interferons:** Trigger antiviral defenses.
5. **Complement:** Opsonization, inflammation, membrane attack.
6. **Inflammation:** Recruits defenses to injury/infection.
7. **Fever:** Elevated temperature set point during systemic response.

**Key idea:** **Innate = rapid, no prior antigen-specific clonal memory.**

sections.title: NK Cytotoxicity, Interferons, and Complement
sections.markdown:
- **NK-cell killing:** **Perforin + granzymes** → programmed target-cell death.
- **Interferons:** Cytokines inducing antiviral states in responsive cells.
- **Complement:** Cascading plasma proteins activated by several routes.
- **C3b:** **Opsonization** (tags for phagocytosis).
- **C3a/C5a:** **Inflammation**; **C5a** recruits leukocytes.
- **C5b–C9:** **Membrane attack complex (MAC)**; damages target membranes.
- **Neutralization:** Antibody blocks toxin/pathogen binding or entry.
- **Opsonization:** Coats target for easier phagocytosis.

**Recall:** **C3b = tag; C5a = recruit; C5b–C9 = punch holes.**

sections.title: Four Cardinal Signs, Inflammation, and Fever
sections.markdown:
**Four cardinal signs:**
- **Rubor = redness:** Increased blood flow.
- **Calor = heat:** Increased blood flow/local activity.
- **Tumor = swelling:** Fluid accumulation.
- **Dolor = pain:** Mediators, injury, pressure.

- **Histamine (mast cells):** Vasodilation and increased vascular permeability.
- **Neutrophils/monocytes:** Recruited to inflammatory sites.
- **Pyrogens:** Alter hypothalamic temperature set point → **fever**.

**Note:** Slide misspells *dolor* and uses a specific fever cutoff; clinical thresholds vary. Memorize the **four Latin signs**.

sections.title: Innate vs Adaptive; Active vs Passive Immunity
sections.markdown:
- **Innate immunity:** Rapid barriers, phagocytes, NK cells, complement; no antigen-specific clonal memory.
- **Adaptive immunity:** **Antigen-specific B/T** responses; supports memory.
- **Humoral immunity:** **B cells/antibodies**.
- **Cell-mediated immunity:** Primarily **T-cell** functions.
- **Active immunity:** Your immune system responds and can form memory.
- **Passive immunity:** Preformed antibodies transferred; usually temporary.

**Four acquired-immunity categories:**
- **Natural active:** Infection/exposure.
- **Artificial active:** Vaccination.
- **Natural passive:** Maternal antibodies (placenta/breast milk).
- **Artificial passive:** Administered antibodies/immune globulin.

**Four adaptive properties:** **Specificity, versatility, memory, tolerance.**

sections.title: MHC I/CD8 vs MHC II/CD4
sections.markdown:
- **MHC I:** On most **nucleated cells**; displays mainly **intracellular peptides** to **CD8 cytotoxic T cells**.
- **MHC II:** On professional antigen-presenting cells (**dendritic cells, macrophages, B cells**); displays mainly **extracellularly acquired peptides** to **CD4 helper T cells**.
- **CD8:** Can kill appropriately recognized infected/abnormal host cells.
- **CD4:** Coordinates immunity; helps activate compatible B-cell responses.

**Pathways:** **Inside cell → MHC I → CD8. Outside antigen taken up → MHC II → CD4.**

**Important:** MHC I itself is normal on healthy nucleated cells; it is **not automatically an infection tag**.

sections.title: B-Cell Activation, Antibodies, and Five Ig Classes
sections.markdown:
**B-cell pathway:** B-cell receptor binds antigen → processes/presents peptide on **MHC II** → matching activated **helper T** support (common protein antigens) → **clonal expansion** → **plasma cells + memory B cells**.

- **Antigen:** Molecule recognized by antigen receptors.
- **Epitope:** Specific recognized molecular feature.
- **Antibody (Ig):** Antigen-binding protein with heavy/light chains.
- **IgM:** Early primary response; commonly pentameric when secreted.
- **IgG:** Major serum/systemic antibody; prominent in secondary responses; crosses placenta.
- **IgA:** **Mucosal secretions**, tears, saliva, breast milk; often dimeric in secretions.
- **IgE:** **Allergy**, mast-cell/basophil effects; some parasite defense.
- **IgD:** **B-cell surface receptor** on many naïve B cells.

**Recall:** **M early; G blood/secondary; A secretions; E allergy; D B-cell display.**

sections.title: Antibody Actions, Titer, and Secondary Response
sections.markdown:
- **Neutralization:** Blocks toxin/pathogen binding or entry.
- **Opsonization:** Coats targets for phagocytosis.
- **Agglutination:** Clumps particles/cells.
- **Precipitation:** Complexes soluble antigens.
- **Complement activation:** Certain antibodies trigger the classical cascade.
- **Antibody titer:** Measure of antigen-specific antibody amount/activity in a sample.
- **Primary response:** First exposure; **slower**, often early **IgM** then IgG.
- **Secondary response:** Re-exposure; generally **faster, stronger, longer**, supported by **memory**; often prominent IgG.

**Exam association:** **Primary = delay; secondary = memory advantage.**

sections.title: Diseases, Anatomy Checklist, and Rapid Recall
sections.markdown:
- **Appendicitis:** Inflamed appendix; rupture can spread infection.
- **HIV:** Infects **CD4-expressing cells**, especially helper T cells.
- **AIDS:** Advanced immune impairment from HIV; not synonymous with any HIV infection.
- **Autoimmunity:** Immune responses against self (lecture examples: **psoriasis, MS, Addison disease, type 1 diabetes**).

**Identify:** Cervical/axillary/inguinal nodes; lymphatic ducts, trunks, cisterna chyli; node **capsule, trabeculae, afferent/efferent, cortex, paracortex, medulla, hilum**; thymus cortex/medulla/Hassall corpuscles; spleen red/white pulp and hilum; palatine/pharyngeal/lingual tonsils; Peyer's patches.

**Rapid pairs:** **Node = filters lymph; spleen = filters blood; thymus = T maturation; bone marrow = B development.** **Afferent arrives; efferent exits.** **MHC I–CD8; MHC II–CD4.** **Right duct = right upper quadrant.** **IgM early; IgG systemic; IgA mucus; IgE allergy; IgD B surface.**

**Instructor question still open:** No single B-cell differentiation hormone identified in the provided slides; **thymosins concern T-cell development**.
